rationale: The book's core identification — that 'righteousness' in Scripture denotes the doing of God's commandments, righteous acts performed and worn, not merely a verdict received — is carried directly by its cited texts. Deuteronomy 6:25 explicitly defines the term ('it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments'), Psalm 119:172 equates the commandments themselves with righteousness, and 1 John 3:7 warns against exactly the deception the book targets ('let no man deceive you: he that doeth righteousness is righteous'). The strongest counter — forensic imputation as the primary sense (Rom 4:3-8; Phil 3:9; 2 Cor 5:21) — cannot explain these three definitional texts without recategorizing them as superseded law-righteousness or merely evidential of an underlying status, both of which are additional unsupported steps that the texts themselves do not take. The book, by contrast, accounts for the counter's best evidence: it affirms that the garment 'was given unto her' (Rev 19:8) and that the deeds are ordained by God (Eph 2:10), so grace and gift are incorporated rather than denied; and the accepted prior premises that faith and belief are themselves obedience-constitutive dissolve the apparent tension with Genesis 15:6 and Romans 4, since faith counted for righteousness is already enacted trust, not bare assent. The Greek of Revelation 19:8 (dikaiōmata, plural righteous acts, so rendered by ASV, ESV, NASB, NIV) decisively supports the garment identification against the KJV's flattened 'righteousness,' and the book's handling of Isaiah 64:6 (the doer is unclean, not the deed) neutralizes the filthy-rags objection. No counter-reading explains the same body of evidence with fewer unsupported steps.
book_core_identification: Righteousness is the doing of God's commandments — righteous acts actually performed (Deut 6:25; Ps 119:172; 1 John 3:7) — such that the scriptural garment of righteousness is woven of deeds done, and righteousness is not reducible to a vague moral quality or a forensic verdict merely received.
book_secondary_elaborations: The garment/fine-linen imagery as covenant-wear: dikaiōmata in Rev 19:8 rendered as 'righteous acts,' the wedding-garment parable read as condemnation for absent deeds
The grace mechanism: the linen 'was given' — deeds fore-ordained by God (Eph 2:10), granted and then worn, so the doing is not self-generated merit
Washing symbolism: baptism as the one bath, foot-washing as daily cleansing of conduct, robes washed in the blood of the Lamb (John 13; Rev 7:14; Zech 3:4)
Nakedness as covenant exposure and fig-leaves as self-made righteousness (Gen 3:7; Prov 14:12; Rev 3:17; 16:15)
The armor of God as God's own war-dress of defined symbols, including the helmet of yeshuah (Isa 59:17; Eph 6:14-17)
The reinterpretation of Isaiah 64:6 — the rag is stained by the sinner's iniquity, not by the act of obedience itself
strongest_counter_interpretation: The classic Protestant forensic reading: righteousness is primarily a legal status credited (imputed) to the believer through faith in Christ apart from works — 'to him that worketh not, but believeth on him that justifieth the ungodly, his faith is counted for righteousness' (Rom 4:5); 'not having mine own righteousness, which is of the law, but that which is through the faith of Christ' (Phil 3:9); 'that we might become the righteousness of God in him' (2 Cor 5:21). On this reading, texts like Deut 6:25 describe a law-covenant righteousness that the gospel supersedes, and 1 John 3:7 describes the evidential fruit of an already-imputed status rather than the definition of righteousness itself.
counter_core_identification: Righteousness is fundamentally a right standing before God declared and credited by grace through faith, of which righteous conduct is a consequence and evidence but not the constitutive substance.
material_core_denial: The counter denies that righteousness is constituted by the doing of God's commandments; it holds that righteousness is a status received apart from works, so that a person is righteous prior to and independent of righteous acts, with deeds functioning only as downstream evidence — the very position the book's entry names and rejects ('a verdict only received').
counter_case: Romans 4:3-8 explicitly says righteousness is 'counted' or 'imputed' 'without works,' to 'him that worketh not, but believeth' — the strongest direct textual claim that righteousness is credited status rather than performed deeds

Philippians 3:9 contrasts 'mine own righteousness, which is of the law' unfavorably with 'the righteousness which is of God by faith,' suggesting law-keeping righteousness is precisely what Paul abandons
2 Corinthians 5:21 says believers 'become the righteousness of God in him,' language of conferred identity rather than accumulated deeds
Genesis 15:6 credits righteousness to Abraham on the basis of belief, before circumcision and before any commanded act in the immediate context
Isaiah 64:6 ('all our righteousnesses are as filthy rags') is traditionally read to disqualify human deeds as the substance of acceptable righteousness
On this reading Deut 6:25 belongs to the Mosaic covenant economy and 1 John 3:7 is evidential: doing righteousness demonstrates, rather than constitutes, being righteous
book_explanatory_advantages: Deuteronomy 6:25 and Psalm 119:172 are explicit lexical definitions of righteousness as commandment-doing; the book takes them at face value while the counter must demote them to a superseded economy — a step the texts nowhere authorize

1 John 3:7 is framed as a warning against deception ('let no man deceive you'), which fits the book's polemic exactly: the deception warned against is precisely the claim that one can be righteous without doing righteousness; the evidential reading blunts the warning's force

Revelation 19:8's dikaiōmata is plural and active ('righteous acts,' so ASV/ESV/NASB/NIV); the book explains why the fine linen at the marriage is deeds, and why the man without the garment is condemned — the imputed reading struggles to explain why the granted garment is defined as the saints' own acts

The book absorbs the counter's grace evidence rather than contradicting it: the linen 'was given,' the deeds are fore-ordained (Eph 2:10), the robe is washed in the Lamb's blood — gift and doing are held together, so Rom 4 and Gen 15:6 are harmonized via the already-accepted premise that faith is itself obedience-constitutive trust

The Isaiah 64:6 objection is answered from the verse's own syntax: 'we are all as an unclean thing' — the stain is the doer's sin, not the deed, which coheres with Isaiah 1:16-18 commanding washing rather than abandonment of doing

The wider garment grammar (Ezek 16 covenant covering then clothing; Zech 3:4; Job 29:14 'I put on righteousness'; Rev 3:4; 16:15; 22:14; Jude 23) consistently treats the garment as conduct kept, defiled, or washed — behavior the imputed-status reading cannot naturally accommodate, since a purely credited status cannot be 'kept' or 'spotted by the flesh' through the wearer's walk

Cross-tradition method consistency: the accepted prior findings on belief, faith, and love (each obedience-constitutive) make the book's account of righteousness the natural fourth member of one coherent covenant vocabulary
counter_explanatory_advantages: Romans 4:4-8's explicit 'without works' and 'worketh not' language is the counter's strongest asset and is not directly exegeted in the supplied proving chapter
Philippians 3:9's disavowal of law-righteousness reads most naturally on the forensic account and receives no explicit treatment in the supplied bundle
The counter matches the dominant historical Protestant consensus, so it explains why the KJV rendering of Rev 19:8 and the mainstream reading of Isa 64:6 arose
decisive_sources: Deuteronomy 6:25 — an explicit scriptural definition: observing to do all the commandments 'shall be our righteousness'
1 John 3:7 — 'let no man deceive you: he that doeth righteousness is righteous,' a warning aimed at the very substitution the book opposes
Revelation 19:8 — dikaiōmata, the plural 'righteous acts of the saints,' identifying the fine linen as deeds while also being 'given,' preserving grace
Isaiah 61:10 with Ezekiel 16:8-10 — the robe of righteousness as covenant covering, then clothing of the covered, establishing the garment grammar the entry summarizes
Revelation 3:4; 16:15; Jude 23 — garments kept, defiled, or spotted by the wearer's walk, intelligible only if the garment is conduct
unresolved_objections: Romans 4:4-8's 'without works' formulation is harmonized only indirectly, via the prior finding that faith is obedience-constitutive; the supplied chapter does not exegete Romans 4 itself
Philippians 3:9's contrast between law-righteousness and faith-righteousness is not directly addressed in the supplied evidence bundle
2 Corinthians 5:21's 'become the righteousness of God in him' receives no treatment; a christological-participation dimension of the term remains under-specified in the entry
The claim that the KJV's 'righteousness of saints' built 'a long confusion' is a historical-theological judgment beyond what the texts alone establish
